method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Clinical review used because the short PMC record titled only 'Relapsing Polychondritis' was under 2,000 characters.

mcqs.question: Which tissues does the review say relapsing polychondritis inflames?

options.A: Elastic cartilage of ear and nose, hyaline cartilage of peripheral joints, axial fibrocartilage, and tracheobronchial cartilage

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Elastic cartilage of ear and nose, hyaline cartilage of peripheral joints, axial fibrocartilage, and tracheobronchial cartilage
mcqs.explanation: Inflammation involves elastic cartilage of the ear and nose, hyaline cartilage of peripheral joints, axial fibrocartilage, and tracheobronchial cartilage.

sourceRefs.excerpt: cartilaginous and proteoglycan-rich tissues, including the elastic cartilage of the ear and nose, the hyaline cartilage of peripheral joints, the fibrocartilage at axial sites and the cartilage of the tracheobronchial tree

mcqs.question: What is the most common presenting pair of features?

options.A: Auricular chondritis and polyarthritis, in over 80%

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Auricular chondritis and polyarthritis, in over 80%
mcqs.explanation: In over 80% of patients the disease is disclosed by auricular chondritis and polyarthritis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In over 80% of patients, RP is disclosed by auricular chondritis and polyarthritis

mcqs.question: How often is another autoimmune disease associated, and which is most common?

options.A: In 30% of adult patients, most often rheumatoid arthritis
options.E: Only in children, most often diabetes

mcqs.correctAnswerText: In 30% of adult patients, most often rheumatoid arthritis
mcqs.explanation: Another autoimmune disorder is found in 30% of adult patients, rheumatoid arthritis being the most common.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Association with other autoimmune disorders is found in 30% of all adult RP patients, rheumatoid arthritis (RA) being the most common.

mcqs.question: What structural airway consequences does the review describe?

options.A: Destruction of tracheal rings, tracheomalacia with airway collapse, and strictures from granulation and fibrosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Destruction of tracheal rings, tracheomalacia with airway collapse, and strictures from granulation and fibrosis
mcqs.explanation: Tracheal-wall thickening destroys cartilage rings. Tracheomalacia may collapse the airway. Strictures develop from granulation tissue and peribronchial fibrosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The thickening of the tracheal wall with destruction of the cartilaginous rings is characteristic. Tracheomalacia may be observed, with resultant airway

mcqs.question: Which interventions does the review say are frequently required for the airway?

options.A: Balloon dilatation, stent placement, tracheotomy, or a combination
options.C: Lung transplant as the first procedure
options.D: No procedural intervention is ever needed

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Balloon dilatation, stent placement, tracheotomy, or a combination
mcqs.explanation: Airway intervention is frequently required by balloon dilatation, stent placement, tracheotomy, or a combination.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Airway intervention is frequently required, by means of balloon dilatation, stent placement, tracheotomy, or a combination
